answers: Review round 7's REQUEST_CHANGES at 8baad29e: two correctness defects in how a round over a gone pod ends, two minors, and the prose that stated the old rule. The architect kept the round Narrow and moved the decision into the machine.

proof.criterion: Item 1. A claim whose process is relaunched into any pod other than the round's own takes no further part in that round: its part is frozen, answered or not, and any ask of that round it holds is dropped rather than sent into the new pod. An answer counts only from a process in the round's pod, so the gone-pod report no longer depends on a sweep reading ErrPodGone before the relaunch.
proof.surface: The claim machines themselves, driven through their own death and relaunch — ScriptResume, observe(runtime.Gone), relaunched() — with the helper asserting the machine moved its own locator rather than a test rewriting it behind the machine's back; and the daemon's sweep over a real PostgreSQL in internal/daemon.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 ./internal/supervise/; and cd packages/daemon && LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5455/postgres?sslmode=disable go test -count=1 -timeout 20m ./internal/daemon/ -run 'PodUpdate|StalePlugin|PodRound|Update|Displaced|Drift'
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/supervise (114.765s) and 37 PASS in internal/daemon. The three new tests: TestPodUpdateAnUnansweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodIsAskedNothingMore (the round's ask is not sent again in the new pod, and an answer posted from there is refused), TestPodUpdateAnAnsweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodKeepsItsAnswer (a turn in the new pod does not take the answer back), and TestPodUpdateAClaimInTheRoundsOwnPodStillLosesItsAnswerToAForeignTurn, the control that the guard is not too wide.
proof.negativeControl: Run with Claim.leftPodRound forced to `return false`, in a throwaway copy of the tree under $TMPDIR and never in the branch: TestPodUpdateAnUnansweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodIsAskedNothingMore fails `prompts sent = 2 ([{DeliveryID:update:pod:9d3f0c7a-… …` — the round's own ask re-sent in the new pod under the same delivery id — and TestPodUpdateAnAnsweredClaimRelaunchedIntoAnotherPodKeepsItsAnswer fails with the answer withdrawn. The control passes in the same run, which is what says the guard is not too wide.

proof.criterion: Item 2. A round, once opened, ends only by replacing its pod or because that pod is gone: there is no third way. completePodUpdate no longer ends a round when no live claim records the round's pod; it asks the runtime about the pod itself and ends only on runtime.ErrPodGone.
proof.surface: The daemon's sweep over a real PostgreSQL with real claim machines, driven through the rig's own operator suspension (letGo clears the locator) landing between the tick's snapshot and the live read, and through the operator's resume back into the same pod.
proof.observed: 37 PASS. TestPodUpdateKeepsARoundWhoseLiveClaimStopsRecordingItsLivePod: nothing replaced, no 'the pod is replaced and the round is over' line, nothing written on the issue, no controller notice, the round and the answer still on the claim, and the operator's resume lets the next sweep replace the pod and end the round. TestPodUpdateEndsTheRoundWhenTheRuntimeSaysItsUnrecordedPodIsGone: the round ends through endRoundOverAGonePod exactly once, with nothing written on the issue because every worker had answered, and no ReplacePod call.
proof.negativeControl: Run with the old fall-through restored, in the same throwaway copy: TestPodUpdateKeepsARoundWhoseLiveClaimStopsRecordingItsLivePod fails `the sweep logged the pod replaced 1 times having replaced nothing: [… msg:supervise: every worker of this update round has answered; the pod is replaced and the round is over …]`, and TestPodUpdateEndsTheRoundWhenTheRuntimeSaysItsUnrecordedPodIsGone fails `the sweep ended the round over a gone pod 0 times, want once`.

proof.criterion: Item 3. PodDrift tells this round's own ReplacePod suspension from a launch's replacement of the same pod. ReplacePod writes a mark of its own, legion.dev/round-displaced-pod, and PodDrift reads that one; a launch's replacement answers runtime.ErrPodGone, so the round ends as a gone pod and the issue is told what went with the disk.
proof.surface: The sandbox runtime against the package's fake dynamic client, with both replacements driven through their real callers — ReplacePod itself, and a Resume into a pod dialing the stream the daemon left, which is the drift that makes a launch replace an issue pod where it stands — read in the window where the Sandbox is suspended and the pod still terminating.
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox (276.593s). TestPodDriftTellsTheRoundsOwnReplacementFromALaunchs covers both: the round's own replacement in flight answers no reasons and no error, a launch replacing the same pod answers runtime.ErrPodGone. TestPodDriftReadsASuspendedSandboxAsItsOwnReplacementOrAsAGonePod keeps its earlier cases and gains a launch-suspended one. TestReplacePodNamesTheDisplacedPodAndWaitsItOut asserts both marks, and the untouched launch and observe tests prove legion.dev/displaced-pod is still written by both acts for the readers that report displaced roles.
proof.negativeControl: Run with PodDrift reading the shared displacedAnnotation again, in the same throwaway copy: TestPodDriftReadsASuspendedSandboxAsItsOwnReplacementOrAsAGonePod fails `PodDrift of a pod a launch's replacement suspended the sandbox over = [], <nil>; want runtime.ErrPodGone`, and TestPodDriftTellsTheRoundsOwnReplacementFromALaunchs/a_launch_replacing_the_same_pod fails the same way, while its sibling subtest for the round's own replacement passes.

proof.criterion: Item 4. The prose the reviewer listed states the rule rather than the order, now that neither reading has to come first.
proof.surface: The repository's own structural checks over the changed guide and the compiled comments.
proof.command: cd /legion/workspaces/sjawhar/legion/infra-484 && bun scripts/semantic-line-breaks.ts docs/kubernetes.md; and cd packages/daemon && gofmt -l ./internal/ && go vet -tags e2e ./... && go build ./...
proof.observed: semantic-line-breaks exits 0; gofmt prints nothing; vet clean; build ok. The four sites now say that whichever reading a sweep reaches first ends the round and the report is the same either way: podupdate.go's reconcileIssuePodUpdate doc, runtime.go's ErrPodGone doc, docs/kubernetes.md's gone-pod passage (which also gains item 2's ending), and podupdate_test.go's comment on the second reading, which had conceded the window.
proof.negativeControl: Before this round the same four passages asserted the opposite — that the round must end at the runtime's reading because the relaunch window would otherwise let the new pod's processes decide the report — and the reviewer cited each of them as prose the fix falsifies. drift.go's own paragraph was corrected in item 3's commit, where the code it describes changed.

filesChanged: packages/daemon/internal/supervise/machine.go, table.go, delivery.go and podupdate_test.go: Claim.leftPodRound and the five places that honour it, with three tests driving the machine's own death and relaunch.
packages/daemon/internal/daemon/podupdate.go and podupdate_test.go: roundWithNoProcessInItsPod, the removal of the fall-through ending, and two tests; plus the sweep doc's rewrite.

packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/relaunch.go, drift.go and drift_test.go: roundDisplacedAnnotation, the replacementKind suspendDisplacing takes, PodDrift reading the round's own mark, and the two tests.
trickyParts: A claim with no locator at all is deliberately not leftPodRound. launchAfter persists a launching claim without one before the Resume that gives it one, and nothing is known then about the pod it will come up in, so its part in the round must stand exactly as it was. Making the predicate true for a locatorless claim would freeze every claim of every relaunch, which is the opposite error.

sendPending drops only an ask of the round the claim has left (updatesRound), not every pending delivery: the rule freezes the claim's part in the round, not its work, so a left-round claim holding an ordinary phase task still gets it.

In roundWithNoProcessInItsPod, a snapshot that records no claim in the round's pod either is itself the evidence that the claims record another pod in its place, so that case ends through the same endRoundOverAGonePod rather than through a second ending written for it.

legion.dev/round-displaced-pod is never cleared and needs no clearing: once the round's pod ends, PodDrift's own pod check answers ErrPodGone before the suspension branch is reached, and a launch can only suspend a running Sandbox, whose pod is by then a different one from any round mark names. replaceSupersededSandbox still carries only the old mark across its delete-and-create, which is right: that is the mark whose readers must span the gap, and a round mark could not outlive a pod that is already gone.
deviations: Three of the round's four commits were written by task(agent="deep-worker") subagents, one at a time, and every one of their reported checks was re-run by the implementer before the commit was made; the prose commit is the implementer's own. No subagent's report was taken as evidence.
CI had not concluded at the code head when this phase completed. The implementer does not wait on CI, and the reviewer reads the head's checks on GitHub before it approves.
